    Glossary

    Terms used across the course and the program, from A to Z.

    Term Meaning
    A/B test Showing two versions to randomly split users to see which performs better on a chosen metric
    AARRR Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue: the stages of a growth funnel
    Acceptance criteria Conditions a feature must meet to count as done, often written as Given / When / Then
    Account Aggregator RBI-regulated system that lets people share their financial data between institutions, with consent
    Activation The moment a new user first gets real value from a product
    Agent (AI) An AI system that plans and takes steps using tools such as APIs or search
    Agile Working in short cycles with frequent feedback instead of one big upfront plan
    AMFI Association of Mutual Funds in India: the industry body that registers mutual fund distributors and publishes monthly industry data, including SIP numbers
    AML Anti-money-laundering: checks that stop financial products being used to hide illegal money
    API An agreed way for two software systems to exchange requests and responses
    ARPU Average revenue per user
    Backlog The ordered list of work a team might do
    BaFin Germany’s federal financial regulator
    CAC Customer acquisition cost: spend on winning customers ÷ new customers
    Churn Share of users or customers who stop using or paying in a period
    CKYC India’s central KYC registry, so investors don’t repeat KYC with every institution
    Cohort A group of users who started in the same period, tracked together over time
    Context window The maximum amount of text an AI model can consider at once
    Conversion rate Users who complete a step ÷ users who reach it
    Counter-metric A metric that catches harm caused by pushing another metric
    DAU / MAU Daily and monthly active users; DAU ÷ MAU measures stickiness
    Demat account An account holding securities electronically, at NSDL or CDSL
    Direct plan A mutual fund plan bought straight from the fund house or a direct platform, with no distributor commission, so its expense ratio is lower
    Discovery Finding out which problems are real and worth solving, before building
    DORA The EU’s Digital Operational Resilience Act for financial firms
    DPDP Act India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
    Epic A large piece of work split into several user stories
    EU Blue Card A German work and residence permit for qualified workers with a job offer above a set salary
    Eval A structured test of an AI system’s output quality
    Exit load A charge for selling mutual fund units within a set period after buying them
    Expense ratio (TER) A mutual fund’s yearly running cost as a share of its assets, taken out of the NAV
    Expiry The date a futures or options contract ends
    F&O Futures and options: derivative contracts traded on exchanges
    Fake-door test A button or page for a feature that doesn’t exist yet, used to measure interest
    Feature flag A switch that turns a feature on or off for some users without a new release
    Fine-tuning Training an AI model further on your own examples
    Funnel The sequence of steps users go through, with drop-off at each step
    GDPR The EU’s General Data Protection Regulation
    Go / no-go A launch decision based on criteria agreed in advance
    Golden dataset Real examples with expected outputs, used to evaluate an AI system
    Guardrail metric A metric that must not get worse while you improve the main one
    Hallucination AI output that sounds right but is false or made up
    Hypothesis A testable prediction: if we change X, metric Y will move by Z, because of R
    ICE A prioritisation score: Impact × Confidence × Ease
    Input metric A lever the team can move, which in turn drives the north-star metric
    INVEST Qualities of a good user story: independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small, testable
    Investment adviser (SEBI) A SEBI-registered person or firm allowed to give investment advice for a fee
    JTBD Jobs-to-be-done: the progress a user is trying to make in a situation
    Kanban A continuous-flow way of working that limits work in progress
    Kano model Sorts features into basics, performance features and delighters
    Kill switch A control that instantly disables a feature or an algorithm
    KPI Key performance indicator: a metric used to track progress
    KYC Know your customer: verifying a customer’s identity
    Latency The time a system takes to respond
    Lebenslauf A German-style CV: newest first, with month and year for every role; usually sent with a cover letter (Anschreiben)
    LLM Large language model: an AI trained on text to generate text
    LLM-as-judge Using one AI model to grade another model’s outputs against a rubric
    LTV Lifetime value: the revenue a customer brings over the whole relationship
    Margin Money a trader must deposit to hold a leveraged position
    MiFID II EU rules for investment services and markets
    MoSCoW Must, Should, Could, Won’t: a way to fix the scope of a release
    Mutual fund distributor A person or firm registered with AMFI that sells mutual funds and earns commission from the fund house
    MVP Minimum viable product: the smallest version that tests whether an idea delivers value
    NAV Net asset value: the price of one unit of a mutual fund, worked out each business day
    North-star metric The one metric that best captures the value delivered to users
    NPCI National Payments Corporation of India, which runs UPI
    OKR Objectives and key results: a goal plus measurable results that show it’s achieved
    Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) A German permit to stay up to 12 months and look for work, based on points or a recognised qualification
    Opportunity solution tree A map from one outcome to user opportunities, solutions and experiments
    p95 The value 95% of measurements fall below, for example response time
    p-value The probability of a result at least this extreme if there were no real effect
    Persona A description of a typical user, ideally based on research
    PMLA India’s Prevention of Money Laundering Act
    Post-mortem A blameless review of an incident: what happened, why, and what to change
    PRD Product requirements document: what is being built, for whom, and how success is measured
    Product–market fit When a product meets strong demand, shown by retention and organic growth
    Prompt injection Hidden instructions in content that try to hijack an AI model
    PSD2 The EU’s second Payment Services Directive: open banking and strong customer authentication
    RACI Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed: who does what
    RAG Retrieval-augmented generation: fetching relevant documents and adding them to an AI prompt
    Regular plan A mutual fund plan sold through a distributor, whose commission is paid from a higher expense ratio
    Research analyst (SEBI) A SEBI-registered person or firm allowed to provide research and recommendations
    Retention The share of users who keep coming back over time
    Retro A team review of what went well, what didn’t, and what to change
    RICE A prioritisation score: Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort
    Roadmap The plan of what a team will work on, best organised by outcomes
    Sample size The number of users a test needs to detect an effect reliably
    SEBI Securities and Exchange Board of India, the securities market regulator
    Segment A group of users who share a need or behaviour
    SIP Systematic investment plan: a fixed amount invested in a mutual fund at regular intervals, usually monthly
    SLA Service level agreement: a promised level of service, such as uptime
    Sprint A fixed period, often 1–2 weeks, in which a Scrum team completes planned work
    Stakeholder Anyone affected by, or able to affect, your product decisions
    STAR Situation, Task, Action, Result: a structure for behavioural interview answers
    Story points A relative estimate of the size of a piece of work
    T+1 Settlement one trading day after the trade
    TAM / SAM / SOM Total, serviceable and obtainable market size
    Tech debt Shortcuts in code that make future changes slower or riskier
    Temperature A setting that controls how random an AI model’s output is
    Token A chunk of text an AI model reads or writes; usage and price are counted in tokens
    UPI Unified Payments Interface: India’s real-time payment system, run by NPCI
    User story “As a [user], I want [capability], so that [benefit]”
    Vanity metric A number that looks good but doesn’t guide any decision
    Velocity How much work a Scrum team completes per sprint, in story points
    WIP Work in progress
